title: Identifying potential biomarkers for type 2 diabetes in the adipose tissue of older adults via multiple machine learning algorithms.
summary: The full primary article identifies AIM2 and FHOD3 as candidate adipose-tissue T2D biomarkers by intersecting LASSO, SVM-RFE and RF, with GEO expression analyses and qPCR in aged/high-fat-fed mice.
ai_technology: three GEO transcriptomic datasets, ML feature intersection, small 65/35 human-data split, then mouse tissue qPCR and diet/age comparisons.

evidence.tested: The human held-out set is only 11 samples and biological follow-up is in mice; approve narrowly as exploratory candidate biomarkers, not validated human diagnostic targets.
evidence.unknown: The reviewed source does not establish prospective benefit, broad external validity, or replication beyond the reported study.
evidence.ai_role: three GEO transcriptomic datasets, ML feature intersection, small 65/35 human-data split, then mouse tissue qPCR and diet/age comparisons.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
